# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1282
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1282
- **Title**: fix(1280): CLI arch matrix gates the merge; release binaries boot-smoked
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1280-linux-arm-binary` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +173
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T11:29:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T12:23:19Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1280

## Diagnosis (AC3 — root cause, FILE:LINE from job logs)

v1.0.512 shipped with **no** fa-linux-\*/windows CLI assets. Chain, from the release run [37268915954](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37268915954) (head fc23b43fe):

1. **Trigger (flake, not toolchain/dep):** `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` (job 111631545548, runner ubuntu-24.04-arm) failed in `test/integration/secret_sheet_test.dart:194` — `TimeoutException after 0:01:30.000000: Timed out waiting for "[Model]" in output` via `pty_harness.dart:355 waitForText` → `pty_harness.dart:294 waitForBoot`. Same head fc23b43fe was **green** 8 min earlier (v1.0.511 run 37268285156) and green again on cf703b3cf — loaded-arm-runner boot flake, not a dart toolchain or native-dep failure.
2. **Starvation:** quality-gate went red → the release `binaries` matrix (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:2627-2630`, `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` gate) was **skipped** whole (job 111672097165 = skipped) → release shipped without `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz`/`fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`/`fa-windows-x64.zip`/`SHA256SUMS`. The arm64 build itself is healthy: v1.0.511 built `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz` green from the same commit.
3. **Never-again gap (NG1, this PR's fix):** the PR-side arch matrix **never gated a merge at all**. `binaries-pr` fired only on `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (old ci.yml:3157), but merge-blocking validations are SM-dispatched as `workflow_dispatch` on the PR head — verified on dispatched run 37145568633 (ai/gh-1198): both `Binaries (PR)` and `Binaries smoke gate` jobs = **skipped**, so the required "Binaries smoke gate" context (machine-sm.yml:78) went green-by-skip on every real validation run. A broken arch build could never block a merge.
4. **NG2 gap:** the release `binaries` job uploaded assets without ever running them (no smoke step between build and upload).

## Change (minimal, scoped to the linux-arm CLI binary leg + the arch-matrix guard)

- `binaries-pr` + `binaries-smoke-gate` also fire on `workflow_dispatch` — the event the merge gate actually rides. On dispatched runs the classifier already treats everything as affected, so the full 5-leg matrix (incl. linux/arm64 on the native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner + `fa --help` smoke) runs exactly when validation is due; docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip. Release arms (push/tag/release/schedule) stay skip.
- Release `binaries` job: new boot-smoke step (`fa --help` must print) **before** Archive/Upload — every shipped arch is proven to boot on its own runner (NG2).
- New guard `test/ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`: both matrices carry the full 5-leg arch inventory, linux/arm64 stays pinned to `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (no cross-compile), the release job smokes before archiving/uploading, and machine-sm keeps stamping the exact "Binaries smoke gate" context.

Failing-first proof: the guard's assertions were mirrored 1:1 and run against pre-fix ci.yml → RED on exactly the 3 fixed assertions; post-fix → ALL GREEN (see below why the dart run itself is deferred to CI).

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: AC2 (NG1 wired — arch matrix + aggregate run on the merge-gating dispatches; machine-sm already requires the context, no protection change needed), NG2 (release boot smoke), AC3 (root cause above + posted on the issue), guard test.
Remaining / noted: the one-off flake itself (`secret_sheet_test` waitForBoot under arm-runner load) is test-infra, green at head, not touched here (shared PTY harness is hot with sibling lanes); v1.0.512's missing assets need an SM-side re-dispatch of its tag run (CI scheduling is not ours); #1267 N4 (merge-snapshot gate) remains the long-term home — pointer posted there.

## Local gates honesty

`dart test`/`dart analyze` are SIGKILLed on this box right now (machine guard, exit 137 on every attempt — not a test failure). No local dart gate was run; verification above is static (ruby YAML mirror of the guard's assertions, RED→GREEN) + this PR's CI as the real gate. `dart format` likewise could not run; the test file is hand-formatted to convention. Threshold files: threshold not touched.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:

{
  "key": "pr-1282",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(1280): CLI arch matrix gates the merge; release binaries boot-smoked",
    "description": "Fixes #1280

## Diagnosis (AC3 — root cause, FILE:LINE from job logs)

v1.0.512 shipped with **no** fa-linux-\*/windows CLI assets. Chain, from the release run [37268915954](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37268915954) (head fc23b43fe):

1. **Trigger (flake, not toolchain/dep):** `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` (job 111631545548, runner ubuntu-24.04-arm) failed in `test/integration/secret_sheet_test.dart:194` — `TimeoutException after 0:01:30.000000: Timed out waiting for "[Model]" in output` via `pty_harness.dart:355 waitForText` → `pty_harness.dart:294 waitForBoot`. Same head fc23b43fe was **green** 8 min earlier (v1.0.511 run 37268285156) and green again on cf703b3cf — loaded-arm-runner boot flake, not a dart toolchain or native-dep failure.
2. **Starvation:** quality-gate went red → the release `binaries` matrix (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:2627-2630`, `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` gate) was **skipped** whole (job 111672097165 = skipped) → release shipped without `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz`/`fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`/`fa-windows-x64.zip`/`SHA256SUMS`. The arm64 build itself is healthy: v1.0.511 built `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz` green from the same commit.
3. **Never-again gap (NG1, this PR's fix):** the PR-side arch matrix **never gated a merge at all**. `binaries-pr` fired only on `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (old ci.yml:3157), but merge-blocking validations are SM-dispatched as `workflow_dispatch` on the PR head — verified on dispatched run 37145568633 (ai/gh-1198): both `Binaries (PR)` and `Binaries smoke gate` jobs = **skipped**, so the required "Binaries smoke gate" context (machine-sm.yml:78) went green-by-skip on every real validation run. A broken arch build could never block a merge.
4. **NG2 gap:** the release `binaries` job uploaded assets without ever running them (no smoke step between build and upload).

## Change (minimal, scoped to the linux-arm CLI binary leg + the arch-matrix guard)

- `binaries-pr` + `binaries-smoke-gate` also fire on `workflow_dispatch` — the event the merge gate actually rides. On dispatched runs the classifier already treats everything as affected, so the full 5-leg matrix (incl. linux/arm64 on the native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner + `fa --help` smoke) runs exactly when validation is due; docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip. Release arms (push/tag/release/schedule) stay skip.
- Release `binaries` job: new boot-smoke step (`fa --help` must print) **before** Archive/Upload — every shipped arch is proven to boot on its own runner (NG2).
- New guard `test/ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`: both matrices carry the full 5-leg arch inventory, linux/arm64 stays pinned to `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (no cross-compile), the release job smokes before archiving/uploading, and machine-sm keeps stamping the exact "Binaries smoke gate" context.

Failing-first proof: the guard's assertions were mirrored 1:1 and run against pre-fix ci.yml → RED on exactly the 3 fixed assertions; post-fix → ALL GREEN (see below why the dart run itself is deferred to CI).

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: AC2 (NG1 wired — arch matrix + aggregate run on the merge-gating dispatches; machine-sm already requires the context, no protection change needed), NG2 (release boot smoke), AC3 (root cause above + posted on the issue), guard test.
Remaining / noted: the one-off flake itself (`secret_sheet_test` waitForBoot under arm-runner load) is test-infra, green at head, not touched here (shared PTY harness is hot with sibling lanes); v1.0.512's missing assets need an SM-side re-dispatch of its tag run (CI scheduling is not ours); #1267 N4 (merge-snapshot gate) remains the long-term home — pointer posted there.

## Local gates honesty

`dart test`/`dart analyze` are SIGKILLed on this box right now (machine guard, exit 137 on every attempt — not a test failure). No local dart gate was run; verification above is static (ruby YAML mirror of the guard's assertions, RED→GREEN) + this PR's CI as the real gate. `dart format` likewise could not run; the test file is hand-formatted to convention. Threshold files: threshold not touched."
  }
}

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Verify tag matches pubspec version
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          echo "tag=$tag pubspec=$version"
          if [ "$tag" != "$version" ]; then
            echo "Tag v$tag does not match pubspec version $version"
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          # dart build cli produces: <output>/bundle/{bin/fah, lib/*.dylib}
          # We rename the executable to `fa`, write version.txt, then archive
          # the whole bundle so the installer can extract bin/ + lib/ together.
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-1280 NG2: «compiles» is not «works» — every release arch boots its
      # binary before the asset is archived/uploaded (same smoke as
      # binaries-pr).
      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

      - name: Archive bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
            cd build/out && 7z a -tzip "../../$asset" bundle && cd -
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
            tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1282
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1282
- **Title**: fix(1280): CLI arch matrix gates the merge; release binaries boot-smoked
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1280-linux-arm-binary` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +173
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T11:29:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T12:23:19Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1280

## Diagnosis (AC3 — root cause, FILE:LINE from job logs)

v1.0.512 shipped with **no** fa-linux-\*/windows CLI assets. Chain, from the release run [37268915954](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37268915954) (head fc23b43fe):

1. **Trigger (flake, not toolchain/dep):** `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` (job 111631545548, runner ubuntu-24.04-arm) failed in `test/integration/secret_sheet_test.dart:194` — `TimeoutException after 0:01:30.000000: Timed out waiting for "[Model]" in output` via `pty_harness.dart:355 waitForText` → `pty_harness.dart:294 waitForBoot`. Same head fc23b43fe was **green** 8 min earlier (v1.0.511 run 37268285156) and green again on cf703b3cf — loaded-arm-runner boot flake, not a dart toolchain or native-dep failure.
2. **Starvation:** quality-gate went red → the release `binaries` matrix (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:2627-2630`, `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` gate) was **skipped** whole (job 111672097165 = skipped) → release shipped without `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz`/`fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`/`fa-windows-x64.zip`/`SHA256SUMS`. The arm64 build itself is healthy: v1.0.511 built `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz` green from the same commit.
3. **Never-again gap (NG1, this PR's fix):** the PR-side arch matrix **never gated a merge at all**. `binaries-pr` fired only on `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (old ci.yml:3157), but merge-blocking validations are SM-dispatched as `workflow_dispatch` on the PR head — verified on dispatched run 37145568633 (ai/gh-1198): both `Binaries (PR)` and `Binaries smoke gate` jobs = **skipped**, so the required "Binaries smoke gate" context (machine-sm.yml:78) went green-by-skip on every real validation run. A broken arch build could never block a merge.
4. **NG2 gap:** the release `binaries` job uploaded assets without ever running them (no smoke step between build and upload).

## Change (minimal, scoped to the linux-arm CLI binary leg + the arch-matrix guard)

- `binaries-pr` + `binaries-smoke-gate` also fire on `workflow_dispatch` — the event the merge gate actually rides. On dispatched runs the classifier already treats everything as affected, so the full 5-leg matrix (incl. linux/arm64 on the native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner + `fa --help` smoke) runs exactly when validation is due; docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip. Release arms (push/tag/release/schedule) stay skip.
- Release `binaries` job: new boot-smoke step (`fa --help` must print) **before** Archive/Upload — every shipped arch is proven to boot on its own runner (NG2).
- New guard `test/ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`: both matrices carry the full 5-leg arch inventory, linux/arm64 stays pinned to `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (no cross-compile), the release job smokes before archiving/uploading, and machine-sm keeps stamping the exact "Binaries smoke gate" context.

Failing-first proof: the guard's assertions were mirrored 1:1 and run against pre-fix ci.yml → RED on exactly the 3 fixed assertions; post-fix → ALL GREEN (see below why the dart run itself is deferred to CI).

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: AC2 (NG1 wired — arch matrix + aggregate run on the merge-gating dispatches; machine-sm already requires the context, no protection change needed), NG2 (release boot smoke), AC3 (root cause above + posted on the issue), guard test.
Remaining / noted: the one-off flake itself (`secret_sheet_test` waitForBoot under arm-runner load) is test-infra, green at head, not touched here (shared PTY harness is hot with sibling lanes); v1.0.512's missing assets need an SM-side re-dispatch of its tag run (CI scheduling is not ours); #1267 N4 (merge-snapshot gate) remains the long-term home — pointer posted there.

## Local gates honesty

`dart test`/`dart analyze` are SIGKILLed on this box right now (machine guard, exit 137 on every attempt — not a test failure). No local dart gate was run; verification above is static (ruby YAML mirror of the guard's assertions, RED→GREEN) + this PR's CI as the real gate. `dart format` likewise could not run; the test file is hand-formatted to convention. Threshold files: threshold not touched.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),

  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via

  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.

    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:

          - runner: macos-15-intel

          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64

            os: linux

        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

        shell: bash

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)

          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"

          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"

          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"

  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.

    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1282
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1282
- **Title**: fix(1280): CLI arch matrix gates the merge; release binaries boot-smoked
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1280-linux-arm-binary` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +173
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T11:29:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T12:23:19Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1280

## Diagnosis (AC3 — root cause, FILE:LINE from job logs)

v1.0.512 shipped with **no** fa-linux-\*/windows CLI assets. Chain, from the release run [37268915954](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37268915954) (head fc23b43fe):

1. **Trigger (flake, not toolchain/dep):** `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` (job 111631545548, runner ubuntu-24.04-arm) failed in `test/integration/secret_sheet_test.dart:194` — `TimeoutException after 0:01:30.000000: Timed out waiting for "[Model]" in output` via `pty_harness.dart:355 waitForText` → `pty_harness.dart:294 waitForBoot`. Same head fc23b43fe was **green** 8 min earlier (v1.0.511 run 37268285156) and green again on cf703b3cf — loaded-arm-runner boot flake, not a dart toolchain or native-dep failure.
2. **Starvation:** quality-gate went red → the release `binaries` matrix (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:2627-2630`, `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` gate) was **skipped** whole (job 111672097165 = skipped) → release shipped without `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz`/`fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`/`fa-windows-x64.zip`/`SHA256SUMS`. The arm64 build itself is healthy: v1.0.511 built `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz` green from the same commit.
3. **Never-again gap (NG1, this PR's fix):** the PR-side arch matrix **never gated a merge at all**. `binaries-pr` fired only on `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (old ci.yml:3157), but merge-blocking validations are SM-dispatched as `workflow_dispatch` on the PR head — verified on dispatched run 37145568633 (ai/gh-1198): both `Binaries (PR)` and `Binaries smoke gate` jobs = **skipped**, so the required "Binaries smoke gate" context (machine-sm.yml:78) went green-by-skip on every real validation run. A broken arch build could never block a merge.
4. **NG2 gap:** the release `binaries` job uploaded assets without ever running them (no smoke step between build and upload).

## Change (minimal, scoped to the linux-arm CLI binary leg + the arch-matrix guard)

- `binaries-pr` + `binaries-smoke-gate` also fire on `workflow_dispatch` — the event the merge gate actually rides. On dispatched runs the classifier already treats everything as affected, so the full 5-leg matrix (incl. linux/arm64 on the native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner + `fa --help` smoke) runs exactly when validation is due; docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip. Release arms (push/tag/release/schedule) stay skip.
- Release `binaries` job: new boot-smoke step (`fa --help` must print) **before** Archive/Upload — every shipped arch is proven to boot on its own runner (NG2).
- New guard `test/ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`: both matrices carry the full 5-leg arch inventory, linux/arm64 stays pinned to `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (no cross-compile), the release job smokes before archiving/uploading, and machine-sm keeps stamping the exact "Binaries smoke gate" context.

Failing-first proof: the guard's assertions were mirrored 1:1 and run against pre-fix ci.yml → RED on exactly the 3 fixed assertions; post-fix → ALL GREEN (see below why the dart run itself is deferred to CI).

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: AC2 (NG1 wired — arch matrix + aggregate run on the merge-gating dispatches; machine-sm already requires the context, no protection change needed), NG2 (release boot smoke), AC3 (root cause above + posted on the issue), guard test.
Remaining / noted: the one-off flake itself (`secret_sheet_test` waitForBoot under arm-runner load) is test-infra, green at head, not touched here (shared PTY harness is hot with sibling lanes); v1.0.512's missing assets need an SM-side re-dispatch of its tag run (CI scheduling is not ours); #1267 N4 (merge-snapshot gate) remains the long-term home — pointer posted there.

## Local gates honesty

`dart test`/`dart analyze` are SIGKILLed on this box right now (machine guard, exit 137 on every attempt — not a test failure). No local dart gate was run; verification above is static (ruby YAML mirror of the guard's assertions, RED→GREEN) + this PR's CI as the real gate. `dart format` likewise could not run; the test file is hand-formatted to convention. Threshold files: threshold not touched.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}

    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

          sdk: stable

      - name: Verify tag matches pubspec version
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          echo "tag=$tag pubspec=$version"
          if [ "$tag" != "$version" ]; then

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

          # the whole bundle so the installer can extract bin/ + lib/ together.

          # App token so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          # gh-1192 AC3: pin the tag to the bump commit the push event
          # carried. head_commit.id is frozen at event time; a default
          # checkout can land on a main that moved in the seconds between the
          # bump push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178
          # interloper that way). tag_release.sh validates the sha (exact
          # bump subject + matching pubspec version) before tagging and
          # refuses to tag a moving HEAD when nothing qualifies.
          BUMP_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
        run: bash scripts/tag_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. 2. **Starvation:** quality-gate went red → the release `binaries` matrix (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:2627-2630`, `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` gate) was **skipped** whole (job 111672097165 = skipped) → release shipped without `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz`/`fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`/`fa-windows-x64.zip`/`SHA256SUMS`. Release arms (push/tag/release/schedule) stay skip.

- New guard `test/ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`: both matrices carry the full 5-leg arch inventory, linux/arm64 stays pinned to `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (no cross-compile), the release job smokes before archiving/uploading, and machine-sm keeps stamping the exact "Binaries smoke gate" context.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}

    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Verify tag matches pubspec version
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          echo "tag=$tag pubspec=$version"
          if [ "$tag" != "$version" ]; then
            echo "Tag v$tag does not match pubspec version $version"
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:

          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          # dart build cli produces: <output>/bundle/{bin/fah, lib/*.dylib}
          # We rename the executable to `fa`, write version.txt, then archive
          # the whole bundle so the installer can extract bin/ + lib/ together.
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi

      # binary before the asset is archived/uploaded (same smoke as
      # binaries-pr).
      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

      - name: Archive bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
            cd build/out && 7z a -tzip "../../$asset" bundle && cd -
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
            tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle

Actually GitHub Actions bash run uses `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` by default, so `-e` IS set! With `-e`, a failing compound command `[ cond ] && assignment` as a standalone command... Under `set -e`, a command that fails causes exit — but there's an exception: commands in `&&`/`||` lists except the last. The whole line `[ ... ] && bin=...` — the shell exits if a *pipeline* fails, except when it's part of a && list... Actually the rule: set -e does not exit if the failing command is part of a && or || list (any position except the command following the final &&/||? no). The exception applies to any command in a && || list except the command following the final && or ||. So `[ false ] && bin=x` — the test is part of an AND list, and it's not the last command... the last command is `bin=x`. If `[ false ]` fails, the list fails; set -e: "The shell does not exit if the command that fails is ... any command in a && or || list except the command following the final && or ||". The test command IS in the list and is not following the final &&, so it's exempt → no exit. The list returns 1 but set -e doesn't trigger. And it's not the last line of the script, so the script continues. OK so it's fine — this is a common idiom. Same pattern used in binaries-pr smoke presumably. Also `out=$("$bin" --help)` — if fa --help exits nonzero, with -e the script exits with that code → step fails. Good. But if `--help` writes to stderr and returns empty stdout... they echo and check non-empty. Fine.

Windows: on windows-latest runner, shell: bash — Git Bash. `out=$(fa.exe --help)` fine.

84:  changes:
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"

- **PR #**: 1282
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1282
- **Title**: fix(1280): CLI arch matrix gates the merge; release binaries boot-smoked
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1280-linux-arm-binary` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +173
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T11:29:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T12:23:19Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1280

## Diagnosis (AC3 — root cause, FILE:LINE from job logs)

v1.0.512 shipped with **no** fa-linux-\*/windows CLI assets. Chain, from the release run [37268915954](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37268915954) (head fc23b43fe):

1. **Trigger (flake, not toolchain/dep):** `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` (job 111631545548, runner ubuntu-24.04-arm) failed in `test/integration/secret_sheet_test.dart:194` — `TimeoutException after 0:01:30.000000: Timed out waiting for "[Model]" in output` via `pty_harness.dart:355 waitForText` → `pty_harness.dart:294 waitForBoot`. Same head fc23b43fe was **green** 8 min earlier (v1.0.511 run 37268285156) and green again on cf703b3cf — loaded-arm-runner boot flake, not a dart toolchain or native-dep failure.
2. **Starvation:** quality-gate went red → the release `binaries` matrix (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:2627-2630`, `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` gate) was **skipped** whole (job 111672097165 = skipped) → release shipped without `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz`/`fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`/`fa-windows-x64.zip`/`SHA256SUMS`. The arm64 build itself is healthy: v1.0.511 built `fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz` green from the same commit.
3. **Never-again gap (NG1, this PR's fix):** the PR-side arch matrix **never gated a merge at all**. `binaries-pr` fired only on `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (old ci.yml:3157), but merge-blocking validations are SM-dispatched as `workflow_dispatch` on the PR head — verified on dispatched run 37145568633 (ai/gh-1198): both `Binaries (PR)` and `Binaries smoke gate` jobs = **skipped**, so the required "Binaries smoke gate" context (machine-sm.yml:78) went green-by-skip on every real validation run. A broken arch build could never block a merge.
4. **NG2 gap:** the release `binaries` job uploaded assets without ever running them (no smoke step between build and upload).

## Change (minimal, scoped to the linux-arm CLI binary leg + the arch-matrix guard)

- `binaries-pr` + `binaries-smoke-gate` also fire on `workflow_dispatch` — the event the merge gate actually rides. On dispatched runs the classifier already treats everything as affected, so the full 5-leg matrix (incl. linux/arm64 on the native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner + `fa --help` smoke) runs exactly when validation is due; docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip. Release arms (push/tag/release/schedule) stay skip.
- Release `binaries` job: new boot-smoke step (`fa --help` must print) **before** Archive/Upload — every shipped arch is proven to boot on its own runner (NG2).
- New guard `test/ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`: both matrices carry the full 5-leg arch inventory, linux/arm64 stays pinned to `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (no cross-compile), the release job smokes before archiving/uploading, and machine-sm keeps stamping the exact "Binaries smoke gate" context.

Failing-first proof: the guard's assertions were mirrored 1:1 and run against pre-fix ci.yml → RED on exactly the 3 fixed assertions; post-fix → ALL GREEN (see below why the dart run itself is deferred to CI).

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: AC2 (NG1 wired — arch matrix + aggregate run on the merge-gating dispatches; machine-sm already requires the context, no protection change needed), NG2 (release boot smoke), AC3 (root cause above + posted on the issue), guard test.
Remaining / noted: the one-off flake itself (`secret_sheet_test` waitForBoot under arm-runner load) is test-infra, green at head, not touched here (shared PTY harness is hot with sibling lanes); v1.0.512's missing assets need an SM-side re-dispatch of its tag run (CI scheduling is not ours); #1267 N4 (merge-snapshot gate) remains the long-term home — pointer posted there.

## Local gates honesty

`dart test`/`dart analyze` are SIGKILLed on this box right now (machine guard, exit 137 on every attempt — not a test failure). No local dart gate was run; verification above is static (ruby YAML mirror of the guard's assertions, RED→GREEN) + this PR's CI as the real gate. `dart format` likewise could not run; the test file is hand-formatted to convention. Threshold files: threshold not touched.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:

          # App token so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —

          # gh-1192 AC3: pin the tag to the bump commit the push event
          # carried. head_commit.id is frozen at event time; a default
          # checkout can land on a main that moved in the seconds between the
          # bump push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178
          # interloper that way). tag_release.sh validates the sha (exact
          # bump subject + matching pubspec version) before tagging and
          # refuses to tag a moving HEAD when nothing qualifies.
          BUMP_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
        run: bash scripts/tag_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'

    needs: [quality-gate]

    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
